cohort: The study included 950 women admitted for deliveries in maternity wards in the city of Botucatu, Sao Paulo.
finding: A high prevalence of urinary incontinence (49.68%) was found during pregnancy, strongly associated with lifestyle habits, gestational morbidities, parity, and previous caesarean sections.
mod_finding: Previous caesarean sections increased the chance of urinary losses during pregnancy, and delivery via caesarean section increased the chance of UI in subsequent pregnancies.
cross-section timing: During pregnancy, with data collected from women admitted for deliveries.
